before.title: 3.4L (3400) Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant/Oil Leak
before.description: The 3.4L V6 (LA1/3400) used in the Montana is notorious for lower intake manifold gasket failure. GM's original design used a plastic (nylon) gasket carrier and silicone seals that crack and shift with heat cycling, allowing coolant and/or oil to leak. Leaks can be external (coolant dripping, low coolant, overheating) or internal (coolant mixing into the oil, producing a milkshake-colored sludge under the oil cap), and an internal leak left unaddressed can wash bearings and destroy the engine.
before.solution: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets, ideally with the updated Fel-Pro/aluminum-frame gasket set rather than the original plastic-carrier design. Inspect for coolant in the oil; if present, do an oil change immediately after the repair and check bearing condition. Many shops also resurface/clean the mating surfaces and replace the thermostat and coolant while the manifold is off.
symptoms: Milky/foamy residue under oil cap (coolant in oil)

before.title: 4T65E Automatic Transmission Failure (Slipping, Shudder, Hard Shifts)
before.description: The Montana's 4T65E 4-speed automatic is a known weak point, particularly in heat and stop-and-go driving. Common failures include slipping out of gear, a shudder when shifting, harsh or delayed shifts, and loss of certain gears as the 4th-gear clutch hubs de-spline from repeated torque-converter lockup. Heat from city driving accelerates failure, and a fluid leak or low fluid is a frequent contributing cause.
before.solution: Service fluid and filter on schedule; many owners/specialists add an auxiliary transmission cooler to combat heat-related failure. For slipping or shudder, diagnose pressure and solenoid operation first; a worn unit typically requires a rebuild or a remanufactured 4T65E. Address any external leaks (axle seals, side cover) promptly to avoid running low.

before.title: Aftermarket Dorman Steering Knuckle Recall (Loss of Steering Control)
before.description: Replacement steering knuckles sold by Dorman (OE Solutions P/Nos. 697-902 and 697-903) and under NAPA P/Nos. 7-8502/7-8503, used on Montana and related GM minivans, were recalled in 2009 because a material/design defect could cause the knuckle to break in the hub area, resulting in sudden loss of steering control and a possible crash without warning. Dorman recalled the affected knuckles, replaced them free of charge, and reimbursed labor (hotline 1-800-523-2492). Owners unsure of part origin should have a shop verify the knuckle.

before.title: Blower Motor / HVAC Blower Resistor Failure
before.description: The Montana's heater/AC blower commonly fails due to a bad blower motor resistor or the blower motor itself. A classic symptom is the fan working only on the highest setting (which bypasses the resistor) while lower speeds are dead; in other cases the blower quits entirely or, less often, runs full-speed and won't shut off. Corrosion at the resistor connector is a frequent contributor.
before.solution: If only high speed works, replace the blower motor resistor (located near the blower motor, usually accessible behind dash trim). Test for power at the blower connector: power present but no fan means a bad motor; no power means a bad resistor (or relay/connector). Inspect and clean corroded connectors and check the relay and ground. Both repairs are inexpensive and require no programming.
symptoms: Blower only works on highest speed
No air from vents / blower dead
Blower runs constantly and won't shut off (resistor/relay)

before.title: Fuel Pump / Fuel System Failure Causing Stalling and No-Start
before.description: Montanas frequently develop fuel-delivery problems: in-tank fuel pump failure and clogged fuel filters cause hard starting, long crank times, intermittent stalling, and no-start conditions. A common pattern is the engine stalling when hot and restarting only after it cools, due to low fuel pressure. Corrosion at the fuel-tank-to-body wiring harness can also trigger a Check Engine Light or crank/no-start.
before.solution: Test fuel pressure to confirm; replace the in-tank fuel pump module if pressure is low and replace the fuel filter (recommended every ~30,000 miles to prevent overstressing the pump). Inspect and repair any corroded fuel-tank harness connectors. Rule out the fuel pump relay and crankshaft position sensor for intermittent stalling.
symptoms: Stalling, often when hot, restarts after cooling
Check Engine Light from fuel tank harness corrosion

before.title: Instrument Cluster / Speedometer Stepper Motor Failure
before.description: Like many GM vehicles of this era, the Montana's instrument cluster suffers from failing Switec/Juken stepper motors and bad solder joints. Gauges — most often the speedometer, but also tach, fuel, and temperature — read erratically, stick, peg, or stop moving entirely. The odometer/gear-position digital display can also dim, flicker, or go dark. This is a widely documented design weakness, though no GM recall covers it.
before.solution: Send the cluster to a specialist (or DIY) to replace all gauge stepper motors with new Switec 27x.168 units and re-flow the solder joints. Because mileage is stored in the cluster, repair the existing unit rather than swapping in a used cluster from another vehicle, which would import the donor's mileage.
symptoms: Gauge needles pegged or not moving

before.title: Power Sliding Door Can Open While Vehicle Is Moving (NHTSA Recall)
before.description: Montana minivans equipped with the passenger-side power sliding door were subject to a safety recall (NHTSA 01V-067 / GM Campaign 01013 and a follow-up) for inadequate front welds on the door actuator. If a weld fails, the actuator can jam in the unlatched position so the door does not latch when closed, allowing the power sliding door to open while driving — especially on hills, turns, or rough roads. An unbelted occupant could fall out.
before.solution: Have the recall performed at a GM dealer: dealers inspect the actuators by date code and replace as needed, and inspect/repair latch anchor wires of improper diameter. Owners can check their VIN on NHTSA's recall site to confirm completion; the repair is free under recall.
symptoms: Power sliding door opens while driving
Door fails to latch when closed
Door not staying shut on turns or bumps
